The per-task pattern reveals why \texttt{bbq\_sauce} is hardest: the BBQ sauce bottle is positioned behind a cluster of tall obstacles (moka pot, wine bottle), requiring the end-effector to navigate through a narrow corridor. \texttt{chocolate\_pudding}, placed at the front of the basket with fewer obstructions, is easiest. \section{Null Distribution and Permutation Test}\label{sec:appendix_null}

We construct the null distribution from all conditions where SDF supervision is either absent or demonstrably redundant ($p > 0.1$ versus LoRA-only). This yields six per-seed CAR values: three LoRA-only seeds and three $\lambda{=}0.005$ seeds (Table~\ref{tab:null_dist}).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{Null distribution construction. Values are per-seed overall CAR (\%) at the 30K checkpoint.}
\label{tab:null_dist}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
Condition & s0 & s1 & s2 & Mean \\
\midrule
LoRA-only & 57.0 & 52.5 & 55.0 & 54.83 \\
LoRA+SDF $\lambda{=}0.005$ & 57.0 & 54.0 & 52.5 & 54.50 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{l}{Pooled null: $\{57.0, 52.5, 55.0, 57.0, 54.0, 52.5\}$} \\
\multicolumn{4}{l}{$\mu_0 = 54.67$, $\sigma_0 = 2.04$} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Permutation test procedure.}
For each treatment condition (e.g., $\lambda{=}0.1$, $k$ seeds), we enumerate all $\binom{6+k}{k}$ ways to draw $k$ values from the combined pool of null + treatment values. The one-tailed $p$-value is the fraction of combinations whose mean $\geq$ the observed treatment mean; the two-tailed $p$-value counts combinations whose deviation from the pooled mean exceeds the observed deviation.

\paragraph{Results for $\lambda{=}0.01$ (3 seeds).}
Treatment values: $\{57.0, 57.5, 54.5\}$, mean = 56.33. Pooled with null: 9 values, $\binom{9}{3} = 84$ combinations. The observed mean (56.33) is within the null range ($p > 0.1$, two-tailed), confirming no significant departure.

\paragraph{Results for $\lambda{=}0.1$ (2 seeds).}
Treatment values: $\{58.0, 58.5\}$, mean = 58.25. Pooled with null: 8 values, $\binom{8}{2} = 28$ combinations. One-tailed $p = 0.036$; two-tailed $p \approx 0.071$. The $z$-score relative to the null is $(58.25 - 54.67)/2.04 = 1.76$. We report the conservative two-tailed value in the main text; a directional prior is justified because SDF is designed to \emph{reduce} collisions.


\section{SSR/TSR Ratio Analysis}\label{sec:appendix_ssr}

The Safe Success Rate (SSR) counts episodes that are both task-successful \emph{and} collision-free. The SSR/TSR ratio measures what fraction of task-completing episodes also avoid collisions. An increase indicates that fine-tuning improves safety among successful trajectories, not merely by suppressing task completion.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{SSR/TSR ratio across conditions. All values computed over 200 episodes (50 per task $\times$ 4 tasks).}
\label{tab:ssr_tsr}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
Condition & Seed & TSR (\%) & SSR (\%) & SSR/TSR \\
\midrule
Pi0.5 baseline & -- & 71.5 & 28.0 & 0.392 \\
\midrule
LoRA-only & s0 & 51.5 & 29.5 & 0.573 \\
LoRA-only & s1 & 51.5 & 27.0 & 0.524 \\
LoRA-only & s2 & 51.5 & 26.5 & 0.515 \\
\midrule
$\lambda{=}0.005$ & s0 & 55.5 & 30.0 & 0.541 \\
$\lambda{=}0.005$ & s1 & 50.5 & 24.0 & 0.475 \\
$\lambda{=}0.005$ & s2 & 56.0 & 29.5 & 0.527 \\
\midrule
$\lambda{=}0.01$ & s0 & 52.5 & 32.5 & 0.619 \\
$\lambda{=}0.01$ & s1 & 55.5 & 30.0 & 0.541 \\
$\lambda{=}0.01$ & s2 & 53.5 & 28.0 & 0.523 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The Pi0.5 baseline achieves SSR/TSR\,=\,0.39: most task-completing trajectories collide. After LoRA fine-tuning, SSR/TSR increases to 0.51--0.57 (mean 0.54), confirming that the CAR improvement reflects genuine avoidance among active trajectories, not reduced exposure from lower TSR. SDF conditions show comparable SSR/TSR ranges ($\lambda{=}0.005$: 0.48--0.54; $\lambda{=}0.01$: 0.52--0.62), reinforcing the conclusion that SDF supervision does not improve the safety profile beyond what LoRA fine-tuning provides.


\section{Displacement Threshold Sensitivity}\label{sec:appendix_threshold}

The displacement-filtered CAR (dfCAR) excludes episodes where the end-effector displacement falls below a threshold $\tau_d$. Table~\ref{tab:threshold_sens} demonstrates that dfCAR is robust across five orders of magnitude of $\tau_d$ for all fine-tuned conditions, because these models exhibit no action collapse (all episodes have displacement $> 0.27$\,m).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\caption{dfCAR (\%) at varying displacement thresholds $\tau_d$. All fine-tuned conditions (LoRA-only and SDF-augmented) show identical CAR across $\tau_d \in [2, 200]$\,mm because no episodes exhibit sub-threshold displacement. Only at $\tau_d = 300$\,mm do 1--2 episodes per condition fall below threshold, causing $\leq$\,0.5\,pp change.}
\label{tab:threshold_sens}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccccccc}
\toprule
$\tau_d$ (mm) & 2 & 5 & 10 & 50 & 100 & 200 & 300 \\
\midrule

For the Pi0.5 baseline (without LoRA), all 200 episodes have EE displacement $> 0.27$\,m (mean 0.37\,m), so dfCAR $\equiv$ CAR $= 28.5\%$ at any reasonable threshold. The bimodal displacement distribution that motivates dfCAR arises in the Pi0 full fine-tuning setting (reported in the main text), where action collapse produces a mode near zero displacement.


\section{Stepwise Checkpoint Ablation ($\lambda{=}0.1$)}\label{sec:appendix_stepwise}

To test whether $\lambda{=}0.1$ produces a sustained training signal rather than a transient fluctuation, we evaluated six checkpoints spanning steps 16K--28K (every 2K steps) for two seeds (s0, s1). The mean CAR across these checkpoints is 55.3\%, within 0.3$\sigma$ of the null distribution mean (54.67\%, $\sigma = 2.04$). No monotonic trend is observed, and individual checkpoint CARs fluctuate within the null band. This suggests that the elevated CAR observed at the 30K checkpoint reflects stochastic variation rather than a sustained geometric-supervision effect.


\section{SDF Ground Truth Pipeline}\label{sec:appendix_sdf_pipeline}

\paragraph{Mesh processing.}
For each SafeLIBERO scene, we extract all visual meshes from the MuJoCo XML model. The \texttt{spatial\_bowl} scene contains 68 meshes (19 initially watertight); \texttt{object\_chocolate} contains 60 meshes (13 initially watertight). We apply automated repair (hole filling, normal correction, winding order fix) via Trimesh, successfully repairing 2/49 and 4/47 non-watertight meshes respectively. Robot arm meshes (complex multi-part geometry) remain non-watertight and are excluded from SDF computation, as the SDF field targets scene obstacles only.

\paragraph{SDF computation.}
Query points are sampled via dual-scale Gaussian ($\sigma_1{=}0.025$, $\sigma_2{=}0.008$, 80\% near-surface) plus 20\% uniform within the bounding box, yielding 4,084 points per scene. SDF values are truncated to $[-0.05, 0.05]$\,m. Key statistics: near-surface ratio ($|$SDF$| < 0.02$) is 61.0--61.5\%; inside ratio (SDF $< 0$) is 20.4--23.8\%.

\paragraph{Gradient verification.}
We verify SDF gradient directions via finite differences ($\epsilon = 10^{-4}$) on 300 near-surface points per scene. Accuracy: 98.7\% (\texttt{spatial\_bowl}), 99.7\% (\texttt{object\_chocolate}). The gradient points away from obstacle surfaces, ensuring that the collision cost $\text{ReLU}(-\text{SDF} + m)$ correctly penalizes proximity.

\paragraph{Sign convention.}
The pysdf library uses positive-inside convention. We apply $\text{SDF} = -\text{pysdf\_output}$ to convert to the standard negative-inside convention. Verified: inside points yield SDF $< 0$ (cost $> 0$); outside points beyond margin yield cost $= 0$.


\section{Training Hyperparameters}\label{sec:appendix_hyperparams}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering

\section{Evaluation Protocol and Metrics}\label{sec:appendix_eval_protocol}

\paragraph{Task descriptions.}
All four tasks require picking up a target object and placing it in a basket, amid Level-II safety obstacles. The tasks are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
    \item \texttt{chocolate\_pudding}: Pick up chocolate pudding, place in basket.
    \item \texttt{orange\_juice}: Pick up orange juice, place in basket.
    \item \texttt{milk}: Pick up milk, place in basket.
    \item \texttt{bbq\_sauce}: Pick up BBQ sauce, place in basket.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Metrics.}
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
    \item \textbf{TSR} (Task Success Rate): fraction of episodes where the task is completed.
    \item \textbf{CAR} (Collision Avoidance Rate): fraction of episodes with no collision detected (contact force $>$ 0.001\,m displacement between any robot link and obstacle).
    \item \textbf{dfCAR} (displacement-filtered CAR): CAR computed only over episodes with EE displacement $\geq \tau_d$ (default $\tau_d = 0.1$\,mm).
    \item \textbf{SSR} (Safe Success Rate): fraction of episodes that are both successful and collision-free.
\end{itemize}
